zh.question: 长大只是身体变大吗？蝌蚪、毛毛虫和蝗虫的成长路线有什么不同？
zh.observe: 分别观察蛙的四肢与尾巴、蝶蛹内部及羽化后的翅膀准备；进入并排比较，切换身体、食物、呼吸和运动四个角度。两侧进度独立，不按同样天数或大小对齐。

academic.title: 同一个体，连续发育；两种案例，不同时间
academic.body: 本页保留蛙的连续形态变化和蝴蝶的阶段观察，并以共同问题比较生活方式。典型蛙类的后腿先明显可见，前腿随后露出，四肢与尾巴会共存；尾吸收涉及调控的细胞死亡、组织分解与材料回收。蛙苗只是变态后的幼体，还需继续生长到性成熟。蝴蝶的卵、幼虫、蛹、成虫也是同一个体的阶段；循环回到卵表示繁殖产生下一代，而不是成年个体倒退。配对按钮只对齐问题，不把两种动物的年龄、体长或持续时间设为相同。

academic.title: 结构改变与取食、呼吸、运动互相联系
academic.body: 外形变化只是发育的一部分。蛙的口部与消化道调整，鳃、皮肤和肺的气体交换贡献发生变化；肺功能在有些蝌蚪阶段就已出现，不是四肢长好才突然开启。蝴蝶幼虫通过取食积累储备，蛹期外部活动减少但代谢与组织重塑持续；并非所有组织溶为一团无结构的液体。昆虫的气门与气管系统不同于蛙的肺。羽化后的翅需要体液辅助展开并逐渐硬化；可见翅膀并不表示立即适合飞行。

academic.title: 比较路线，不用一条路线概括所有动物
academic.body: 蝴蝶卵—幼虫—蛹—成虫的路线是昆虫完全变态；蝗虫卵—若虫—成虫的路线没有独立蛹期，属于昆虫不完全变态。若虫通常与成虫较相似，在多次蜕皮中继续发育；这些昆虫类别不用于给蛙归类。部分蛙直接在卵内发育，没有自由游泳的蝌蚪期。食谱、寄主植物、发育速度也依物种和环境变化。第三案例仅为路线图，蛹透视是解释图；图形不提供解剖测量、统一发育天数或真实运动模拟。

zh.misconception: 蛙尾逐渐吸收，不是整条掉下；蛹仍在发育，不是在睡觉。不是所有变态都有蛹，蛙也不属于昆虫完全／不完全变态的分类。
zh.boundary: 代表性、放大的形态示意，不对应特定物种的天数、大小或器官测量。部分蛙直接发育、没有自由游泳蝌蚪；蝴蝶各阶段是同一个体的观察快照，不是连续解剖重建。图中蛙苗还需生长成熟，下一代卵来自之后的繁殖。观察野生动物请留在原处，不触碰蛹或翅。

narration.label: 长大不只是变大
narration.text: 先看看池塘里的卵。孵出来的蝌蚪有长尾巴，却和岸边的青蛙很不一样。再去叶片上看看蝴蝶的卵，它出来的是毛毛虫，不是小翅膀蝴蝶。我们跟着两只不同的小动物，各自记住成长进度，看看身体会带来哪些新本领。
narration.cue: 分别访问蛙和蝶的幼体观察，再回到蛙。

narration.label: 腿长出来，尾巴还在
narration.text: 把蛙的进度慢慢往前推。先看后腿，再找前腿。现在停一停：四条腿已经出现，尾巴还在！尾巴会慢慢被身体吸收，一些材料重新利用，不是整条掉到水里。最后出现的蛙苗还没成熟，它以后还要继续长大。
narration.cue: 暂停在四肢与尾巴共存处，再缓慢观察尾吸收。

narration.label: 蛹里不是睡大觉
narration.text: 来到蝴蝶这边，选中蛹并打开内部示意。外面安静，里面却在继续发育。幼虫攒下的储备帮助身体变化。选成虫后再慢慢观察翅膀：先小而皱，再展开，还要等它逐渐硬化。画面让我们看清步骤，并不是蝴蝶真实生活只需要这么几秒。
narration.cue: 揭示蛹内部，再播放和暂停羽化后的独立翅膀进度。

narration.label: 同一个问题，不同的答案
narration.text: 把两只动物并排看，换成食物、呼吸或运动，你发现什么？它们不是同时出生、同样快长大。再看蝗虫的路线：卵、若虫、成虫，中间没有蛹。原来动物有不同的成长方法。观察真实小动物时，让它留在自己的家里，不去碰脆弱的蛹和翅膀。
narration.cue: 进入比较页，切换四个角度，最后观察蝗虫无蛹路线图。

en.question: Is growing up only getting bigger? How do tadpole, caterpillar and grasshopper routes differ?
en.observe: Inspect the frog's limbs and tail, the butterfly's pupa diagram and wing preparation. Compare body, food, breathing and movement side by side. Each animal has an independent timeline, not equal days or sizes.

academic.title: One individual develops; two cases keep separate clocks
academic.body: The frog's continuous morphology and butterfly stage observations address shared questions. In a common frog route, hind limbs become visible before forelimbs emerge, with limbs and tail briefly coexisting. Tail resorption involves regulated cell death, tissue breakdown and reuse of material. A froglet still needs to grow to sexual maturity. Butterfly egg, larva, pupa and adult are also one individual's stages; returning to eggs denotes reproduction and the next generation. Comparison presets align questions, not equal age, body size or developmental duration.

academic.title: Body changes connect feeding, breathing and movement
academic.body: Visible form is only part of development. Frog mouth and digestive structures change, as do the contributions of gills, skin and lungs to gas exchange. Lung function can begin in tadpoles, rather than switching on when limbs are complete. Caterpillars accumulate reserves; pupae remain metabolically active while tissues remodel. Not every tissue dissolves into an unstructured liquid. Insect spiracles and tracheae differ from frog lungs. After emergence, fluid helps wings expand and the wings must harden; visible wings are not necessarily flight-ready.

academic.title: Compare routes without making one route universal
academic.body: Butterfly egg–larva–pupa–adult development is complete metamorphosis in insects. Grasshopper egg–nymph–adult development has no distinct pupa and is incomplete metamorphosis. Nymphs typically resemble adults more closely and develop through repeated moults. These insect categories are not used here to classify frogs. Some frogs develop directly without free-swimming tadpoles. Diet, host plants and timing vary with species and conditions. The third case is a route diagram, and the pupa interior is explanatory—not anatomical measurement, universal timing or a physical movement simulation.

en.misconception: Frog tails are resorbed rather than dropped, and pupae keep developing rather than simply sleeping. Not all metamorphosis includes a pupa; insect complete/incomplete categories do not classify frogs here.
en.boundary: Enlarged, representative illustrations, not species-specific days, sizes or organ measurements. Some frogs develop directly without free-swimming tadpoles. Butterfly stages revisit one individual's life, not a continuous anatomical reconstruction. Froglets still need to mature; the next generation's eggs result from later reproduction. Observe wild animals in place; do not touch pupae or wings.

narration.label: More than getting bigger
narration.text: Begin with eggs in a pond. A tadpole hatches with a long tail and looks unlike a frog on the bank. On a leaf, a butterfly egg hatches into a caterpillar, not a miniature winged adult. Follow two different animals, each with its own progress, and look for new abilities as their bodies change.
narration.cue: Visit both larval observations, then return to the frog.

narration.label: New legs, a remaining tail
narration.text: Move the frog's progress slowly. Find the hind legs, then the forelegs. Pause: four limbs and a tail can exist together! The tail is gradually resorbed and some material reused, rather than falling into the water. The froglet at the end is not yet mature; it still has growing to do.
narration.cue: Pause with four limbs and a tail, then inspect gradual tail resorption.

narration.label: A pupa is not a long sleep
narration.text: Select the butterfly's pupa and open the inside diagram. A quiet outside hides continuing development, supported by reserves accumulated as a caterpillar. Select the adult and watch its wings: small and crumpled, then expanded, then gradually hardening. Our playback reveals steps, not real development compressed into an actual few seconds.
narration.cue: Reveal the pupa diagram, then play and pause independent wing preparation.

narration.label: One question, different answers
narration.text: Place the two animals side by side and compare food, breathing or movement. They did not start at the same time or grow at the same rate. Look at the grasshopper route too: egg, nymph, adult, with no pupa in between. Animals have different ways of growing. Watch wild animals in place and avoid touching delicate pupae and wings.
narration.cue: Switch the four comparison lenses and inspect the grasshopper no-pupa route diagram.
